title: Adding polynomial fractions
line: Two fractions 1/x and 1/(x+1) slide together, grow a shared bottom x(x+1), and their tops merge into (2x+1).

title: Same rules as 1/2 + 1/3
line: The sum 1/x + 1/(x+1) sits beside 1/2 + 1/3, then x becomes 2 and every piece turns into its number twin.

title: Polynomial division is number division
line: Dividing x² + 3x + 5 by x + 1 runs beside 135 ÷ 11, and setting x = 10 shows identical steps.

title: The leftover that shrinks
line: The curve (x² + 1)/x is split into the line y = x plus 1/x, and the gap between them shrinks as x grows.

title: Sorting strings of x and y
line: All 16 four-letter words of x and y, like xyyx, drop into piles by number of y's, stacking 1, 4, 6, 4, 1.

title: Pascal's triangle by pegs
line: Balls bounce down a peg board and each slot's number is the sum of the two above, building Pascal's triangle row by row.

title: Powers of eleven
line: The numbers 121, 1331 and 14641 line up as Pascal rows, then 11 becomes (10 + 1) and the 11⁵ carries break the pattern.

title: Squaring x + y with tiles
line: A square of side x + y splits into x², two xy rectangles and y², which slide apart and label themselves.

title: Difference of squares cut and slide
line: A 7×7 square loses a 3×3 corner, and the leftover L is cut and slid into a 10×4 rectangle: 49 − 9 = 40.

title: Odd numbers stack into squares
line: L-shaped layers of 1, 3, 5 and 7 dots nest into a 4×4 square, one odd number per layer.

title: A machine for right triangles
line: Picking whole numbers x and y in (x² − y²)² + (2xy)² = (x² + y²)² spits out right triangles 3-4-5, 5-12-13 and 8-15-17.

title: 49 squared in your head
line: A 50×50 square loses two 1×50 strips and gets back a tiny corner, so the counter ticks 2500 − 100 + 1 = 2401.

title: Walking the sign chart
line: A dot walks the x-axis as factors (x + 2), (x − 1), (x − 3) flip sign at each zero, pushing the curve over or under.

title: Bounce or cross
line: At x = 1, the graph of (x − 1) crosses, (x − 1)² bounces, and (x − 1)³ flattens out before crossing.

title: Dragging a root
line: In (x + 1)(x − 2)(x − a), the zero a slides from −3 to 3 and the curve wiggles to stay on all three dots.

title: The remainder is the height
line: As a slides along x³ − 2x + 1, the remainder from dividing by (x − a) always matches the curve's height there.

title: Divide or plug in
line: Synthetic division of x³ − 4x² + x + 6 by (x − 2) races plugging in 2, and both land on 0.

title: Area model meets 13 × 12
line: An (x + 3) by (x + 2) rectangle splits into x², 3x, 2x and 6, then x becomes 10 and the tiles total 156.

title: Polynomials as base-x numbers
line: Adding (x² + 2x + 3) and (4x² + 5x + 6) column by column matches 123 + 456 when x is 10.

title: Zero pairs vanish
line: Algebra tiles for 2x² + x − 3 meet flipped tiles for x² − 2x + 1, and matching opposite pairs pop out of existence.

title: Two angles in a rectangle
line: A triangle with angle β stacks on one with angle α inside a rectangle, and matching opposite sides spell out sin(α + β).

title: Rotate, then rotate again
line: A unit-circle point at angle α turns another β, and its new x-coordinate splits into cos α cos β − sin α sin β.

title: Two waves make a shifted one
line: The waves 0.5 sin x and 0.87 cos x add point by point and land exactly on sin(x + π/3).

title: Squares on a spinning triangle
line: As a point spins around the unit circle, squares on the cos θ and sin θ legs trade area but always total 1.

title: Two waves stack flat
line: The area under sin² x is shaded, then cos² x stacks on top, and together they fill exactly up to y = 1.

title: The quadrant picks the sign
line: Knowing sin θ = 3/5 lights two circle points at height 0.6, with cos θ = ±4/5, and the quadrant picks one.

title: Ferris wheel at 30 meters
line: A line at 30 m cuts the rider's height wave, arcsin finds the first crossing, and symmetry and the period find all the rest.

title: Trimming sine to flip it
line: The sine wave fades everywhere outside −π/2 to π/2, and the piece that survives flips across y = x into arcsin.

title: Cosine needs another window
line: A horizontal line slides up the cosine wave hitting it many times, until everything outside 0 to π is erased and it hits once.

title: Three dials on a wave
line: Dials for amplitude, period and midline twist a sine wave until it fits day lengths of 9 hours in December and 15 in June.

title: Unrolling a Ferris wheel
line: A seat circles a 20 m wheel while its height is traced to the right, drawing a wave centered at the hub.

title: Mirror points on the circle
line: Points at θ and −θ mirror across the x-axis, so heights flip sign while x stays put, making sine odd and cosine even.

title: Twice around, same wave
line: A point loops the unit circle twice, and the second lap's height graph is an exact copy of the first, shifted 2π.

title: Half a square, half a triangle
line: A unit square cut on its diagonal and an equilateral triangle cut in half slide into the circle at π/4, π/6 and π/3.

title: One angle, four reflections
line: The point at π/6 mirrors to π − x, π + x and 2π − x, and the same two coordinates reappear with flipped signs.

title: Wrapping the number line
line: A number line wraps around the unit circle like thread, with 1, 2, 3 up to 6.28 landing in order and negatives wrapping clockwise.

title: Sine past 90 degrees
line: A right triangle's angle grows until the triangle breaks at 90°, but the point on the circle keeps going and its height keeps graphing.

title: Bending the radius
line: A circle's radius peels off and bends onto the edge, marking one radian, then copies follow until six fit with a sliver left over.

title: Same angle, any circle
line: A 60° slice cuts circles of radius 1, 2 and 3, and the arc divided by the radius reads 1.05 every time.

title: Log counts the doublings
line: One cell splits into 2, 4, 8 up to 1024 while a counter ticks the doublings, landing near 9.97 when it passes 1000.

title: Exponent in the mirror
line: The curve 2ˣ reflects across y = x into log₂ x, and the point (3, 8) visibly swaps into (8, 3).

title: Slide rule multiplication
line: Two rulers marked in log spacing slide past each other, and adding the lengths for 2 and 3 lands on the mark for 6.

title: The undo machine
line: The number 3 goes through 'times 2, plus 1' to make 7, then runs backward through 'minus 1, divide by 2' to 3.

title: Folding along y = x
line: The parabola y = x² flips across y = x and fails the vertical line test until its left half is erased.

title: Four knobs on a parabola
line: As k changes, y = x² shifts up, stretches, slides sideways and squeezes for f(x) + k, kf(x), f(x + k) and f(kx).

title: Why plus moves left
line: In f(x + 2), the output from input 0 now appears at x = −2, so every dot slides two steps left.

title: Even and odd by folding
line: The graph of x² folds onto itself along the y-axis, x³ spins half a turn onto itself, and x³ + 1 fails both moves.

title: The determinant is the area
line: A grid bends under the matrix [[2, 1], [0, 1.5]], and the unit square becomes a parallelogram whose area counter reads 3.

title: Squashed flat
line: A matrix morphs until its columns line up, the parallelogram flattens into a segment, and the area counter drops to 0.

title: Flipping the plane over
line: A square with colored corners goes through a matrix with determinant −2, doubling in area with its color order reversed.

title: Follow the basis arrows
line: A matrix moves the two basis arrows, and 2 of the new first plus 1 of the new second lands on the image of (2, 1).

title: Four quarter turns
line: The matrix [[0, −1], [1, 0]] turns the arrow (3, 1) a quarter turn each time, and after four turns it's back home.

title: The do-nothing matrix
line: The identity matrix leaves the grid where it was, then the zero matrix pulls every point into the origin.

title: Some squashes can't be undone
line: A shear is undone by its inverse, but a determinant 0 matrix crushes the grid onto a line that can't be spread back.

title: Order matters for moves
line: Two copies of an F shape get the same rotate and shear, in opposite orders, and end up pointing in clearly different directions.

title: Row meets column
line: A row of one 2×2 matrix tips onto a column of the other, the pairs multiply and add, and one answer entry fills in.

title: Tripling a matrix
line: Every entry of a matrix triples while the parallelogram it makes from the unit square grows 3 times each way, 9 times the area.

title: Counting routes with a matrix
line: Roads between 4 towns light up 1s in a grid, and squaring that grid counts every two-road trip between each pair of towns.

title: Stretch, shrink, flip
line: As c slides from 2 to −1.5, the arrow cv stretches, shrinks to a dot, then flips, its length reading |c| times |v|.

title: Doubling the staircase
line: The arrow (3, 2), drawn as 3 steps right and 2 up, doubles to 6 right and 4 up, pointing the same way.

title: Tip to tail
line: Arrows (3, 1) and (1, 2) chain tip to tail, then in the other order, closing up a parallelogram with one diagonal.

title: Lengths don't just add
line: Arrows of length 3 and 4 swing open, and their sum's length slides from 7 down to 1, passing 5 at a right angle.

title: Subtraction joins the tips
line: The arrow w flips into −w and chains onto v, then slides to show v − w runs from w's tip to v's tip.

title: Rowing across a river
line: A boat rows across at 4 m/s, a 3 m/s current drags it along a 5 m/s diagonal, then it angles upstream instead.

title: Two tugboats, one barge
line: Two tugs pull a barge with ropes at different angles, their force arrows join tip to tail, and the barge moves along the sum.

title: Subtract the starting point
line: An arrow from (1, 2) to (5, 5) slides until its tail sits at the origin, and its tip lands on (4, 3).

title: The arrow that moves around
line: One arrow of length 2 pointing northeast is copied all over the plane, and every copy is the same vector, whatever its position.

title: Where the roots go
line: A parabola rises off the x-axis, and its two roots slide together, meet, then split up and down into the complex plane.

title: A loop that must hit zero
line: A circle of inputs shrinks while its image under z² + 1 is drawn, and somewhere the output loop has to sweep across 0.

title: Factoring a sum of squares
line: The tiles of (x + 2i)(x − 2i) multiply out, the i tiles cancel, and the −4i² corner flips to +4.

title: Finding the hidden roots
line: The parabola x² − 2x + 5 misses the axis, its upside-down twin hits at 1 ± 2, and the roots are 1 ± 2i.

title: Distance as a difference
line: Points 1 + 2i and 4 + 6i are joined, the difference 3 + 4i slides to the origin, and its length reads 5.

title: The midpoint is the average
line: Two complex points pull toward each other at the same speed and meet at their average, which is the middle of the segment.

title: Times i is a quarter turn
line: The point 3 + i, multiplied by i again and again, spins a quarter turn each time and returns after four.

title: Multiplying spins the plane
line: Multiplying the whole complex grid by 1 + i turns it 45° and stretches it by about 1.41, every square staying a square.

title: The conjugate is a mirror
line: A point flips across the real axis to its conjugate, and adding the two pulls a sum straight down onto the real line.

title: Two addresses for one point
line: The point 1 + √3i is reached by walking 1 right and √3 up, then again by turning 60° and walking 2.

title: Conjugates cancel the turn
line: Multiplying by 3 + 4i turns 53° and multiplying by 3 − 4i turns back, so the product lands on 25.

title: FOIL with i
line: A 2×2 grid multiplies out (2 + 3i)(1 + 4i), and the 12i² box flips to −12, leaving −10 + 11i.

title: Halfway to a flip
line: Times −1 spins the number line half a turn, so a number whose square is −1 must be a quarter turn: i.

title: 1000 people take a test
line: In a grid of 1000 dots with 10 sick, a 95% accurate test lights up about 60, and only 10 are sick.

title: Pull the goalie
line: A team down one goal pulls its goalie, and bars for tying the game grow faster than bars for giving up another.

title: Fair flips, bent coin
line: A coin landing heads 70% of the time is flipped twice, and the HT and TH boxes in a probability square match exactly.

title: Is this game worth $1
line: A spinner pays $5, $1 or nothing, and its running average payout over 500 spins settles at $0.80, below the $1 price.

title: Tallies become a distribution
line: Fifty family-size dots stack into bars, the bars rescale until they sum to 1, and a marker slides to the expected value of 3.2.

title: Two dice make a triangle
line: All 36 cells of a 6×6 dice grid slide into columns by their sum, piling into a triangle with 7 at the peak.

title: Waiting for a six
line: Bars for rolling the first six on try 1, 2, 3 each shrink by 5/6, and the balance point lands on 6 rolls.

title: Expected value balances the seesaw
line: Probability bars sit on a seesaw, and the pivot slides until the seesaw stops tipping, at exactly the expected value.

title: Outcomes become numbers
line: Each of the 36 dice pairs sends an arrow to the gap between its numbers, and the arrows pile into bars.

title: The birthday surprise
line: People enter a room one by one, the chance of no shared birthday shrinks each time, and dips below 50% at 23.

title: Counting pairs of marbles
line: Lines join every pair among 3 red and 5 blue marbles, 28 in all, and the 3 red-red lines glow to give 3/28.

title: Splitting a bar twice
line: A bar splits 3/5 for a red first draw, the red part splits 2/4 for a second red, and the leftover sliver is 6/20.

title: Don't count the overlap twice
line: Hearts and face cards fill two circles, 3 cards glow because they're counted twice, and subtracting them leaves 22 out of 52.

title: Zooming into a condition
line: On a 6×6 dice grid, every cell except the 5 that sum to 8 fades away, and the 5 survivors become the new whole.

title: A table becomes a picture
line: A two-way table of 100 students becomes a square cut into strips, whose lines only line up straight if independent.

title: Rescaling the B region
line: In a unit square, region B grows to fill the frame, and the part of A inside it becomes P(A given B).

title: Independence is a straight cut
line: A square cut 0.3 across and 0.6 down leaves a corner of area 0.18, matching 0.3 × 0.6, until the cut bends.

title: Sorting a die into circles
line: The faces 1 to 6 float into circles for 'even' and 'bigger than 3', and the union, overlap and outside light up in turn.

title: Shuffle the labels
line: Twenty plants get their 'fertilized' labels reshuffled 200 times, the gaps pile into a hill, and the real 3 cm gap sits far out.

title: Bigger polls, tighter guesses
line: Polls of 25, 100 and 400 people from a crowd that's 40% blue pile into histograms that get narrower each time the size quadruples.

title: Coin flips pick the groups
line: Sixteen people, some secretly athletes, are split by hand and every athlete lands in one group, then coin flips split them evenly.

title: Is this coin fair
line: A coin gave 16 heads in 20 flips, but 500 runs of 20 fair flips show 16 or more barely ever happens.

title: Tasting the soup
line: One scoop of 100 dots from a jar of 10,000 guesses 27% red, then the jar is revealed to be 30% red.
